title: The Office - Small Talk 6 - Talking About Yourself
audio: mp3/322. The Office - Small Talk 6 - Talking About Yourself.mp3

segments.en: Hello everyone and welcome to EnglishPod.
My name is Catherine and you've probably heard us talking a little bit about small talk the past few weeks.
segments.zh: 我的名字是凯瑟琳，你可能听过我们在过去几周里谈论的一些闲聊。

segments.en: We have another episode about small talk and we're going to teach you some things that you can say to people when you haven't seen them or maybe even met them before.
segments.zh: 我们有另一集关于闲聊，我们将教你一些你可以在你没有见过的人甚至以前见过他们时对他们说的话。

segments.en: Today we're going to talk to a stranger.
segments.zh: 今天我们要和一个陌生人谈谈。

segments.en: So we're going to talk very briefly about some casual topic.
segments.zh: 所以我们将非常简单地讨论一些随意的话题。

segments.en: And so let's jump into the dialogue and see what happens.
segments.zh: 所以让我们跳进对话，看看会发生什么。

segments.en: Excuse me, is this seat taken?
segments.zh: 请问，这个座位有人坐吗？

segments.en: It's much bigger than I imagined and much more exciting.
segments.zh: 比我想象中大多了，也热闹多了。

segments.en: There's so much to see here.
segments.zh: 这里有太多地方可以逛了。

segments.en: It's much more modern than people imagine.
segments.zh: 比很多人想象的现代化得多。

segments.en: I'm from Kansas originally, a much quieter and more peaceful place than here.
segments.zh: 我老家是堪萨斯州，那里比这儿安静平和多了。

segments.en: But I'm living in Paris right now.
So now we're going to take a look at a lot of phrases on this occasion.
segments.zh: 所以现在我们要看看这个场合的很多短语。

segments.en: So let's go for fluency builder part one.
segments.zh: 所以让我们去 Fluency Builder 第一部分。

segments.en: So the first phrase we have is a very common phrase if you're in a train or on a bus.
segments.zh: 因此，如果您在火车上或在公共汽车上，我们的第一个短语是一个非常常见的短语。

segments.en: You hear the phrase, is this seat taken?
segments.zh: 你听到这句话，这个座位被占用了吗？

segments.en: So Michelle came up to the stranger and said, excuse me, is this seat taken?
segments.zh: 于是米歇尔走到陌生人面前说，对不起，这个座位被占用了吗？

segments.en: That means, is anybody sitting here?
segments.zh: 也就是说，有人坐在这里吗？

segments.en: It basically means, can I sit here?
segments.zh: 这基本上意味着，我可以坐在这里吗？

segments.en: This is a very polite way of asking if you can sit down in the seat.
segments.zh: 这是一种非常有礼貌的方式，询问您是否可以坐在座位上。

segments.en: You can also say it in a restaurant, at a movie theater, in a classroom.
segments.zh: 你也可以在餐厅、电影院、教室里说。

segments.en: This was a really, really common phrase.
segments.zh: 这是一个非常非常普遍的短语。

segments.en: So it's a very polite way of saying, can I sit down?
segments.zh: 所以这是一种非常礼貌的说法，我可以坐下吗？
你基本上是在请求许可。

segments.en: Because what if a person says, well, no, it's not.
segments.zh: 因为如果一个人说，好吧，不，不是。

segments.en: Do you have to say, may I sit down?
segments.zh: 你不得不说，我可以坐下吗？

segments.en: Well, if they say, I'm sorry, someone is sitting here.
segments.zh: 好吧，如果他们说，对不起，有人坐在这里。

segments.en: That means that maybe they're waiting for a friend and then no, you can't sit there.
segments.zh: 这意味着他们可能在等一个朋友，然后不，你不能坐在那里。

segments.en: But if they say, sure, like in the dialogue, feel free, then you're really basically able to sit down.
segments.zh: 但如果他们说，当然，就像在对话中一样，感觉自由，那么你基本上可以坐下来。

segments.en: So the stranger answers by saying, no, please feel free.
segments.zh: 所以陌生人回答说，不，请随意。

segments.en: So he says, no, the seat is not taken.
segments.zh: 所以他说，不，座位没有坐。

segments.en: What does he mean by this?
Feel free is a very unusual phrase in English, but one that you're going to hear a lot.
segments.zh: Feel Free 在英语中是一个非常不寻常的短语，但你会经常听到。

segments.en: It basically means do what you want to do.
segments.zh: 它基本上意味着做你想做的事。

segments.en: So if I want to sit down, I say, is this seat taken?
segments.zh: 所以如果我想坐下，我说，这个座位被占用了吗？

segments.en: If you say, feel free, Marco, that means feel free to sit down.
segments.zh: 如果你说，随意，马可，这意味着随意坐下。

segments.en: So we can complete the sentence by saying, no, please feel free to sit down.
segments.zh: 所以我们可以通过说，不，请随意坐下来完成这句话。

segments.en: But it's kind of stating the obvious.
segments.zh: 但这有点说明显而易见的。

segments.en: You're saying basically feel free to do what you want.
segments.zh: 你是说基本上可以随意做你想做的事。

segments.en: But you could use it in other ways.
segments.zh: 但是你可以用其他方式使用它。

segments.en: For example, Hey Marco, are you using this pen right here?
segments.zh: 例如，嘿，马可，你在这里使用这支笔吗？

segments.en: That means feel free to use my pen.
segments.zh: 这意味着随意使用我的笔。

segments.en: And so then they started talking about what they do, where they work.
segments.zh: 然后他们开始谈论他们做什么，他们在哪里工作。

segments.en: And Michelle said, yes, I work in Shanghai.
segments.zh: 米歇尔说，是的，我在上海工作。

segments.en: Now this is a really important construction.
segments.zh: 现在这是一个非常重要的结构。

segments.en: This is a really important phrase in English.
segments.zh: 这在英语中是一个非常重要的短语。

segments.en: And I think a lot of people make mistakes with this.
segments.zh: 而且我认为很多人会因此而犯错误。

segments.en: So how about you means, do you work in Shanghai?
segments.zh: 那么你的意思是，你在上海工作吗？

segments.en: I just said I work in Shanghai, but how about you?
segments.zh: 我只是说我在上海工作，但你呢？

segments.en: So that's saying, and you, do you work here?
segments.zh: 所以这就是说，你，你在这里工作吗？

segments.en: Or and you, what do you do?
Now, the common mistake with how about you or using the construction how about is that for some reason, some people seem to think that it means how is it?
segments.zh: 现在，关于你怎么样或使用结构的常见错误是出于某种原因，有些人似乎认为这意味着它是如何的？

segments.en: So for example, if someone says, how about your weekend?
segments.zh: 例如，如果有人说，你的周末怎么样？

segments.en: But in this case, how about you always follows a statement.
segments.zh: 但在这种情况下，你总是跟随一个陈述怎么样。

segments.en: So yes, I do live in Shanghai.
That means, do you live in Shanghai?
segments.zh: 也就是说，你住在上海吗？

segments.en: If I say, I would like to eat a hamburger and French fries.
segments.zh: 如果我说，我想吃一个汉堡和炸薯条。

segments.en: What would you like to eat?
So remember, that's the way that you use how about.
segments.zh: 所以请记住，这就是您使用的方式。

segments.en: Never say how about your weekend or how about your vacation when you want to ask, how was it?
segments.zh: 永远不要说你的周末怎么样，或者当你想问的时候你的假期怎么样，怎么样？

segments.en: No, basically, this is a way to reply to someone when they're telling you about their experience.
segments.zh: 不，基本上，这是一种在某人告诉您他们的经历时回复您的方式。

segments.en: You want to talk about yours.
Okay, so let's take a break.
Let's review everything and we'll be back with Fluency Builder part two.
segments.zh: 让我们回顾一下一切，我们将带着 Fluency Builder 第二部分回来。

segments.en: Excuse me, is this seat taken?
segments.zh: 请问，这个座位有人坐吗？

segments.en: It's much bigger than I imagined and much more exciting.
segments.zh: 比我想象中大多了，也热闹多了。

segments.en: There's so much to see here.
segments.zh: 这里有太多地方可以逛了。

segments.en: It's much more modern than people imagine.
segments.zh: 比很多人想象的现代化得多。

segments.en: I'm from Kansas originally, a much quieter and more peaceful place than here.
segments.zh: 我老家是堪萨斯州，那里比这儿安静平和多了。

segments.en: But I'm living in Paris right now.
So now let's continue with some more phrases on Fluency Builder.
segments.zh: 所以现在让我们继续介绍一些关于 Fluency Builder 的短语。

segments.en: Okay, this first phrase is one that I really like to use.
segments.zh: 好的，第一个短语是我真正喜欢使用的一个短语。

segments.en: She says, you can say that again.
But she's talking about how Shanghai is so big and so exciting.
segments.zh: 但她说的是上海有多大，如此令人兴奋。

segments.en: And Michelle says, you can say that again.
segments.zh: 米歇尔说，你可以再说一遍。

segments.en: Now, what does this mean, Marco?
segments.zh: 现在，这是什么意思，马可？

segments.en: So she is basically agreeing with the person.
segments.zh: 所以她基本上同意这个人。

segments.en: The stranger says, Shanghai is amazing.
Michelle says, you can say that again.
segments.zh: 米歇尔说，你可以再说一遍。

segments.en: It's saying, I agree with you.
segments.zh: 就是说，我同意你的看法。

segments.en: All right, so this is very emphatic.
segments.zh: 好吧，所以这是非常强调的。

segments.en: That means that it's really, it's more than just I agree.
segments.zh: 这意味着它真的，不仅仅是我同意的。

segments.en: The person really feels something about this, feels passionately about it.
segments.zh: 这个人真的有一些感觉，对此充满热情。

segments.en: So if you go to the movies and you say, oh, that movie was terrible, you can say.
segments.zh: 所以如果你去看电影，你说，哦，那部电影很糟糕，你可以说。

segments.en: Now, when Michelle asked the stranger where he was from, he says, I'm from Kansas originally.
segments.zh: 现在，当米歇尔问陌生人他来自哪里时，他说，我最初来自堪萨斯州。

segments.en: I'm from Kansas originally means maybe I don't live in Kansas now, but that's where I come from.
segments.zh: 我来自堪萨斯州，最初的意思是也许我现在不住在堪萨斯州，但这就是我来自的地方。

segments.en: That means, you know, at the beginning.
segments.zh: 这意味着，你知道，一开始。

segments.en: And remember, Kansas, by the way, is one of the states in the United States.
segments.zh: 请记住，顺便说一句，堪萨斯州是美国的州之一。

segments.en: And so he's saying he's from Kansas, but now he lives in Paris.
segments.zh: 所以他说他来自堪萨斯，但现在他住在巴黎。

segments.en: So that's why you say, I'm originally from Kansas, but I live in Paris.
segments.zh: 所以这就是为什么你说，我来自堪萨斯州，但我住在巴黎。

segments.en: All right, so Marco, you live here in Shanghai, but where do you come from originally?
segments.zh: 好吧，马可，你住在上海，但你最初来自哪里？

segments.en: And I'm originally from Chicago, but I currently live in China.
segments.zh: 我来自芝加哥，但我目前住在中国。

segments.en: And as he was talking about Kansas, he also said that, well, it's obviously a lot quieter and more peaceful.
segments.zh: 当他在谈论堪萨斯时，他也说过，嗯，这显然更安静、更平静。

segments.en: And then he ends his statement by saying, that's for sure.
segments.zh: 然后他最后说，这是肯定的。

segments.en: And this is a phrase that we use to add emphasis on something.
segments.zh: 这是我们用来强调某事的短语。

segments.en: It's almost like saying, this is a really quiet, much quieter and peaceful place.
segments.zh: 这几乎就像说，这是一个非常安静，更安静和宁静的地方。

segments.en: It's not like you're adding anything to the statement, like no meaning, but you're actually kind of making it more strong.
segments.zh: 这不像您在声明中添加任何内容，就像没有意义一样，但您实际上是在让它变得更强大。

segments.en: So obviously, Kansas compared to Shanghai is a lot more quieter.
segments.zh: 所以很明显，堪萨斯与上海相比，安静了很多。

segments.en: Or I could say that in Chicago in the winter, it's a lot colder than Shanghai.
segments.zh: 或者我可以说冬天在芝加哥，它比上海要冷得多。

segments.en: So again, you're emphasizing on your statement, telling everyone that it's very, very much like this.
segments.zh: 再说一次，你强调你的陈述，告诉所有人它非常非常像这样。

segments.en: So that's all the phrases we have for you.
segments.zh: 这就是我们为您准备的所有短语。

segments.en: Why don't we listen to our dialogue one last time.
segments.zh: 我们为什么不上次听我们的对话。

segments.en: It's much bigger than I imagined and much more exciting.
segments.zh: 比我想象中大多了，也热闹多了。

segments.en: There's so much to see here.
segments.zh: 这里有太多地方可以逛了。

segments.en: It's much more modern than people imagine.
segments.zh: 比很多人想象的现代化得多。

segments.en: I'm from Kansas originally, a much quieter and more peaceful place than here.
segments.zh: 我老家是堪萨斯州，那里比这儿安静平和多了。

segments.en: But I'm living in Paris right now.
So small talk with a stranger.
This is actually a very common scenario.
segments.zh: 这实际上是一个非常常见的场景。

segments.en: If in a bus, in a train, you sit next to a stranger, this is more or less what you're going to talk about.
segments.zh: 如果在公共汽车上，在火车上，你坐在陌生人旁边，这或多或少是你要谈论的内容。

segments.en: And you don't even have to talk about this with a total stranger.
segments.zh: 你甚至不必和一个完全陌生的人谈论这个。

segments.en: You could actually use this with someone that you're working with or just an acquaintance.
segments.zh: 您实际上可以与您一起工作的人或只是熟人一起使用它。

segments.en: So basically, these are key questions that you would ask someone that you don't really know very well.
segments.zh: 所以基本上，这些是你会问你不太了解的人的关键问题。

segments.en: And as you can see, you're not really going into any deep personal questions.
segments.zh: 正如你所看到的，你并没有真正进入任何深刻的个人问题。

segments.en: It's very light conversation, very brief as well.
segments.zh: 这是非常轻松的对话，也非常简短。

segments.en: And I would like to add that in American culture, people often think it's very rude to ask someone how much do you earn, how much is your apartment, how much is your car.
segments.zh: 我想补充一点，在美国文化中，人们常常认为问别人你赚多少钱，你的公寓多少，你的车多少是非常粗鲁的。

segments.en: So in small talk in American culture, and I think a lot of Western cultures, we don't talk about money or religion.
segments.zh: 所以在美国文化的闲聊中，我认为很多西方文化，我们不谈论金钱或宗教。

segments.en: So I think it's important to talk about things that are very simple.
segments.zh: 所以我认为谈论非常简单的事情很重要。

segments.en: What do you do for a living?
This is exactly, I think, one of the main points that when you're learning a language such as English, not only to understand the language, but also the culture.
segments.zh: 我认为，这正是您学习英语等语言时的主要观点之一，不仅要理解语言，还要了解文化。

segments.en: It's very, very different, especially, for example, in Asian cultures where it's no big deal if you go to the hairdresser and the hairdresser asks you how much you earn.
segments.zh: 这是非常非常不同的，尤其是在亚洲文化中，如果你去理发店，理发师问你赚了多少钱，这没什么大不了的。

segments.en: But in the United States or many Western countries, it's not something that you talk about your salary or that you really ask.
segments.zh: 但在美国或许多西方国家，这不是你谈论你的薪水或你真正要求的事情。

segments.en: And if you talk about it, you might make people very uncomfortable.
segments.zh: 如果你谈论它，你可能会让人们非常不舒服。

segments.en: And so I recommend talking about some of the things that we've discussed here and some of the things that we've discussed in other lessons in this series about small talk.
segments.zh: 所以我建议谈谈我们在这里讨论的一些事情以及我们在本系列中关于闲聊的其他课程中讨论的一些事情。

segments.en: And if you have any questions or any comments about this lesson, you can come and visit us at EnglishPod.com.
segments.zh: 如果您对本课程有任何疑问或意见，您可以来 englishpod.com 访问我们。

segments.en: We hope to see you guys there.
